boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Missouri-Columbia, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-to-evening first-weekend sequence pairing campus landmarks, student spaces, and public Columbia destinations.

cards.title: Start at the Columns
cards.subtitle: Francis Quadrangle
cards.notes: Begin with a campus-orientation lap around the six surviving columns, then use the Quad as your reference point for the rest of the walk.
cards.short_summary: A historic starting point at Mizzou’s traditional campus heart.
cards.evidence_claim: The six Columns are the remains of Academic Hall after its 1892 fire and stand on Francis Quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use normal campus pedestrian access.

cards.title: Look up at Jesse Hall
cards.subtitle: South end of Francis Quadrangle
cards.notes: Continue to the south end of the Quad for a close look at the dome and the building that anchors Mizzou’s central historic view.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark and the university’s main administration building.
cards.evidence_claim: Jesse Hall is the University of Missouri’s main administration building and is located at the south end of David R. Francis Quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; interior and event access can vary.

cards.title: Get oriented at Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: MU campus community center
cards.notes: Step inside to locate lounges, food options and student-support points, then take a few minutes to choose a comfortable place to regroup.
cards.short_summary: A practical campus stop for services, seating and food options.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Student Union serves as a community center and provides facilities, services and conveniences for students, faculty, staff and university guests.
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual services may vary; purchases are optional.

cards.title: Make a study-space scout
cards.subtitle: 520 S 9th St
cards.notes: Use the library’s floor plans to identify a quiet room, a group-work area or the Digital Media Lab before coursework starts in earnest.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library with mapped study and learning spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Ellis Library is Mizzou’s main library, with floor plans and locations including the Digital Media Lab, Information Commons and Grand Reading Room.
cards.source_title: Ellis Library – Maps, Floor Plans & Directions
cards.access_notes: Check library access information and hours before entering.

cards.title: Browse the art galleries
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, east wing of Ellis Library
cards.notes: Take a self-guided gallery break and follow the museum’s visitor guidance: no food or drinks, no flash photography and no touching artworks.
cards.short_summary: Free galleries spanning ancient objects through contemporary art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Art & Archaeology is in Ellis Library, is open to the community and has free admission.
cards.source_title: Visit & Tours | Museum of Art and Archaeology
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed on university holidays.

cards.title: Explore the anthropology galleries
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Ellis Library
cards.notes: Enter from Lowry Mall, Hitt Street or the main library and take in the human-origins, archaeology and culture-focused displays at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A museum visit centered on human history, archaeology and cultures.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Anthropology, on the lower level of Ellis Library, explores early humans, North American archaeology, peoples and cultures, and archery from six continents.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Museum of Anthropology
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday noon–4 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Check out MizzouRec
cards.subtitle: 1000 Rollins St
cards.notes: Stop by to learn the facility layout and current recreation options, then confirm what access applies to you before planning a workout or court time.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation facilities with schedules that change by area and season.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec publishes separate operating schedules for its facility and amenities, and lists its address as 1000 Rollins St.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current hours page; last admission is 30 minutes before closing and amenity schedules vary.

cards.title: Find Faurot Field
cards.subtitle: Mizzou Sports Park
cards.notes: Walk to the stadium perimeter for a campus-landmark check-in, and use the official campus map when you want to connect it with other destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Faurot Field is listed on the University of Missouri campus map.
cards.access_notes: View from publicly accessible campus routes; event entry requires separate arrangements.

cards.title: Take a lake-loop reset
cards.subtitle: 2001 E Broadway
cards.notes: For an off-campus breather, follow the hard-surface lake or perimeter trail and keep the park’s posted closing time in mind on the way back.
cards.short_summary: A city park with trails, lake views, gardens and public amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Stephens Lake Park has a 0.6-mile hard-surface lake trail and a 1.7-mile hard-surface perimeter trail, and is open 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; follow posted rules and use daylight awareness on trails.

cards.title: Save a daylight hike for Rock Bridge
cards.subtitle: Rock Bridge Memorial State Park
cards.notes: Choose the marked Karst Trail for a longer weekend outing; wear sturdy shoes, stay on the boardwalk and trails, and plan transport back before dark.
cards.short_summary: A marked park route past the natural rock bridge and Devil’s Icebox area.
cards.evidence_claim: Karst Trail is a 1.75-mile moderate loop at Rock Bridge Memorial State Park with boardwalk, viewing platforms and stairs leading to geological features including the natural rock bridge.
cards.source_title: Rock Bridge Memorial State Park Map
cards.access_notes: The official map identifies natural surfaces, steps and potentially slippery conditions; stay on designated routes and plan ahead.
